channel.description: AI first. Everything else that matters, twice a day.

item.title: lordon1a/agents.md: A drop-in AGENTS.md system prompt for coding agents: full execution, no hedging, no moralizing, no…
item.description: A drop-in AGENTS.md system prompt for coding agents, a single 14 KB file meant to stop hedging, moralizing, fading to black and asking permission for requested work. It is written as a constitution rather than a task list. Why it matters: Shows interest in instruction files that change how coding agents behave; it has 66 GitHub stars so far.

item.title: indexable-inc/blaze: Incremental rust builds up to 92x faster than cargo/rustc
item.description: The blaze repo's ra-jit tool runs beside cargo, recompiling only edited functions into a running program for up to 92x faster incremental Rust builds.

item.title: OpenMobile-2 proves open-source smartphone agents can rival proprietary models
item.description: Researchers found that training smartphone agents on more distinct apps, not more data, improves them, and their open OpenMobile-2 model scored highest among open models on SPA-Bench on real Android devices. Why it matters: Open alternatives to proprietary phone agents matter because training data for them is mostly held by big companies.

item.title: China’s tech giants are paying 1 million yuan for a new kind of AI engineer
item.description: Chinese tech giants including ByteDance, Tencent and Alibaba are offering pay approaching 1 million yuan to attract forward-deployed engineers, who work directly with customers to integrate AI applications into business operations. Why it matters: Firms are racing to commercialise AI, and engineers who bridge models and business needs are in high demand.

item.description: At a PAP conference, PM Lawrence Wong said the party will renew itself by refreshing ideas, broadening membership and expanding networks.

item.title: Gas Supply may pursue remedies if contract breached following Indonesia’s export cuts: Tan See Leng
item.description: Singapore's energy minister said Gas Supply will check with suppliers whether Indonesia's gas export cut breached contracts, and will pursue remedies if needed. The cut is under 2% of Singapore's daily gas demand, and replacement gas is sufficient. Why it matters: Energy security and supply contracts matter here; Indonesia's cut is framed as prioritising its own domestic energy needs.
